svg.title: Defence-in-depth pharmaceutical anti-counterfeit stack
svg.desc: Five stacked anti-counterfeit layers with the regulator-mandated GS1 DataMatrix serialization at the base and successive layers above it: Layer 1 GS1 DataMatrix serialization for DSCSA and EU FMD; Layer 2 NFC AES-128 Secure Dynamic Messaging cryptographic per-pack authentication; Layer 3 tamper-evident closure via NTAG 424 DNA TagTamper CTTES or a destructive antenna for EU FMD Article 5; Layer 4 overt security print such as hologram, colour-shift and microtext; Layer 5 covert markers such as taggants and UV ink. A note states each layer defeats a different attack class, so a counterfeiter must defeat all five, and that NFC supplements rather than replaces the mandated DataMatrix.
svg.text: DEFENCE-IN-DEPTH — NFC ON TOP OF MANDATED DATAMATRIX
Each layer defeats a different attack class; the serialization carrier stays mandatory at the base
Hologram, colour-shift ink, microtext — pharmacist visual check
TagTamper CTTES bit or destructive-antenna bridge — peeling breaks the antenna
NTAG 424 DNA AES-128 Secure Dynamic Messaging — per-pack, non-reproducible
Layer 1 · GS1 DataMatrix serialization — MANDATED CARRIER
GTIN + serial + lot + expiry · DSCSA + EU FMD · NFC never replaces this
DataMatrix alone is trivially photocopied and a copied serial passes EMVS until it is decommissioned.
The NFC layer adds per-pack cryptographic proof; the tamper layer defeats label-transfer to a counterfeit pack.
A counterfeiter must defeat every layer — not just the printed barcode.
